Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — Saturday is a light-wind, dry day under high pressure with weak, low thermals: peak thermal strength (w*) at the launches is only about 150-230 ft/min, and thermal tops (height of the mixed layer) mostly stay 500-1,300 ft above ground. Air is only moderately unstable (cools about 6 °C per km of height), so expect soft, gentle thermals rather than punchy ones. Rainbow Ridge is the standout with steady aligned easterly wind and ridge lift helping all morning; most other sites face crossed or tail winds. NWS Reno also expects light winds today, and the model has matched the light overnight winds at valley airports. Compared with the previous run, cloud cover went up at most sites (from 0% to about 24-33%) and Kingsbury lost its thermals.

Site Breakdown

Rainbow Ridge Favorable — Steady easterly wind on launch with ridge lift and the best thermals of the day through late morning and midday.
Window: 9am–2pm
Wind is 8-9 mph from 64-69° from 9am to noon, easing to 4-5 mph from 83-100° by 1-2pm, all within the launch range. Ridge lift of +104 to +129 ft/min from 9am to noon is not enough to soar alone, but it helps alongside thermals of 151-230 ft/min. Thermal tops are 710-990 ft above ground. Wind direction changes up to 43° within 100 m of height near 750 ft above ground (vector shear 7 mph per 100 m), so expect bumpy air near the top of climbs. Landing is only about 500 ft below launch.

Not recommended today (8) — click a row for details

Hallelujah Marginal — Light westerly to southwesterly wind lines up for a few midday hours, but thermals are weak and the wind turns sharply with height.
Window: 12pm–3pm
Thermal strength 189-210 ft/min with thermal tops 870-1,250 ft above ground from noon to 2pm, easing to 159 ft/min at 3pm. Wind is 3-5 mph, from 306° at noon and backing to 224-226° by 1-2pm, near the southern edge of the launch range. Ridge lift of +56 to +123 ft/min is overstated because stable air flows around the lower slope, so don't count on soaring the ridge. Wind direction changes by up to 42° within 100 m (330 ft) of height, so expect turbulent, uneven climbs. No evening soaring: at 4pm the wind is 3 mph from 186°, off launch.
McClellan Marginal — Wind is on launch from late morning, but thermals are weak, tops are low, and there is strong wind shear near the top of the lift.
Window: 11am–2pm
Thermal strength 162-209 ft/min with thermal tops 530-740 ft above ground from 11am to 2pm, so expect little height gain above launch. Wind is 5-7 mph, veering from 123° to 171° and staying on launch. Peak vector wind shear (change in wind speed and direction combined) is 8 mph per 100 m at about 760 ft above ground, and direction changes by 37°, so expect rough air near the top of climbs. Thermals fade to 99 ft/min by 3pm.
West McClellan Marginal — Wind stays slightly south of the launch range, giving only a short, crossed window with weak thermals.
Window: 1pm–3pm
Thermal strength 148-159 ft/min with thermal tops about 670 ft above ground from 1-2pm, dropping to 65 ft/min by 3pm. Wind is 3-5 mph from 209-234°, just south of the 240-300° launch range (cross from the left). The morning south-southeast flow gives sinking air on launch (-38 to -52 ft/min). Vector wind shear peaks at 8 mph per 100 m near 750 ft above ground.
Peavine Mountain Marginal — Wind veers west of the south launch just as thermals become usable, leaving a short window with sinking air on the slope.
Window: 10:30am–11:30am
Thermal strength 95-185 ft/min at 10-11am, peaking at 228 ft/min with a thermal top about 1,300 ft above ground at 1pm. By then, though, wind is 11-12 mph from 241-242°, outside the 135-225° launch range. Wind is 9 mph from 208-228° during the window. Estimated ridge lift is negative from 9am on (-40 to -63 ft/min), so launch sits partly on the lee side of the westerly flow.
Daydreams Marginal — Light wind is roughly on launch in the morning, but thermals are too weak to climb in, so expect mostly sled rides.
Window: 9am–11am
Thermal strength peaks at 106 ft/min at 9am with a thermal top about 540 ft above ground, then holds at only 66-82 ft/min. That is below a paraglider's sink rate of about 200 ft/min. Wind is 2-3 mph from 200-224°, within the launch range, and ridge lift is calm or blocked by stable air. Late afternoon the wind swings to 262-294°, outside the launch range, and the 4pm ridge lift of +124 ft/min comes too close to sunset to use.
Kingsbury grade Unfavorable — Winds are near calm and mostly from the north, off the southeast launch, and the model no longer shows usable thermals.
Thermal strength peaks near 96 ft/min with a thermal top only about 400 ft above ground around 11am-noon, too weak to stay up. Wind is 1-2 mph from 19-55° through midday, outside the 74-134° launch range, and ridge lift is calm. The previous run showed thermals from 10:30am; this run shows none, and cloud cover rose from 0% to 33%.
Slide Mountain Unfavorable — West winds put launch on the downwind side all day, with strong sinking air by afternoon.
Thermal strength peaks at only 57 ft/min at noon. Wind blows from 194-293°, behind or across the south-southeast launch, building to 11-12 mph from 261-275° at 3-4pm. Estimated ridge lift is negative all day (sinking air), reaching -338 to -412 ft/min from 2-4pm.
Duck Hill Unfavorable — Wind blows from the south-southeast all day, a tailwind for the west-to-north launch.
Wind is 7-10 mph from 149-160° from 8am through 4pm, opposite the 270-50° launch range, with negative ridge lift. Thermals reach 173-179 ft/min at 12-1pm, but launch is not usable. No evening soaring: at 4pm the wind is still 7 mph from 151°.

Hazards

  • Low-level wind shear: Several sites show the wind turning or strengthening sharply 580-760 ft above ground. The largest direction changes are 42-43° per 100 m at Hallelujah and Rainbow Ridge, and the largest vector shear is 8 mph per 100 m at McClellan and West McClellan. Expect rough, uneven air near the top of climbs.
  • Lee-side sinking air at Slide and Peavine: Westerly surface flow puts the Slide Mountain and Peavine launches on the downwind side, with estimated sinking air on the slope. Sink reaches -412 ft/min at Slide by 3pm and -71 ft/min at Peavine by 4pm. Expect sink and possible rotor downwind of these ridgelines.
  • Weak thermals and stable air: Thermals mostly peak at 150-230 ft/min with low tops, and stable air keeps much of the slope air from rising at several ridge sites. Many flights may be short sleds, so pick landing options before launching.
  • Morning haze: NWS Reno expects valley inversions and morning haze that may reduce slant visibility near Reno each morning. Visibility is not modeled here.
  • Lee-side and mountain wave risk: low today: Wind at Sierra crest height over Reno stays light, 4-15 knots from 235-261°, well below the roughly 25 knots that typically brings rotor and downslope wind. NWS Reno expects stronger winds around 10,000 ft by early Sunday morning, with brief low-level wind shear and mountain wave turbulence; that is after this forecast day.
